NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>The source shows a two-storey white rectangular building from the front-left: two upper glazed openings, one broad ground-floor opening, two vertically aligned narrow left windows, a projecting glass-railed balcony, a full-height timber strip at the front-right, thin roof edging, grey plinth and projecting paved terrace. CURRENT reproduces these main facade elements, but the upper openings and balcony assembly have incorrect vertical proportions, and the terrace is missing. The supplied source-matched camera still differs in perspective, so apparent building depth alone is not grounds for correction. The rear, right wall and roof surface are unobserved in SOURCE. Screenshots show apparent balcony-to-wall contact but cannot establish whether the joint is physically connected.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: CURRENT upper glazed openings are approximately as tall as the ground-floor opening and start too close to the roof. SOURCE shows shorter upper openings, a deeper wall zone above them, and a higher balcony floor relative to the facade height.
action: Locally lower the upper opening heads and raise their thresholds with the balcony floor, using normalized facade heights in the front-left comparison. Preserve the two-opening arrangement and central mullions.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="front">problem: CURRENT balcony fascia is noticeably thinner than SOURCE’s substantial white slab edge, weakening the projecting balcony silhouette.
action: Increase the slab/fascia thickness downward from the corrected balcony floor. Keep the glass railing seated on the slab and maintain continuous side returns and wall contact.</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="front-left">problem: SOURCE has a paved terrace projecting beyond the front and left walls, including beyond the balcony footprint. CURRENT terminates at a narrow base strip.
action: Add the visible shallow terrace apron locally around the front and left base, retaining the separate grey wall plinth. Its hidden extent remains uncertain.</issue>
<keep>Two vertically aligned narrow openings on the left wall.
Two upper front openings with a central mullion in each.
Broad ground-floor glazing divided into two principal panes.
Full-height narrow timber strip at the front-right edge.</keep>
